body:
Hi @PhoebeHui  @LilyWangL, 

I debugged this last night and have updated the issue with more clarity and a temporary fix via a text replace in the tools.cpp.
Hi @armitagemderivitec, thanks for posting this issue. I can't reproduce this issue on my Linux. Could you please provide your temporary fix steps? Thanks!

Hi @LilyWangL, 

The fix is as follows which was included above: 

```
sed -i 's/get_path(paths, GitProvider())/{\"git\", \"0\"}/g' toolsrc/src/vcpkg/tools.cpp
```

which just replaces `get_path(paths, GitProvider())` with `{"git", "0"}` in tools.cpp making the code flow the same as when `useSystemBinaries` flag was passed in the bootstrap. 

Are you passing the `useSystemBinaries` on bootstrap?

@LilyWangL if you are familiar with docker you can create the exact image of the server I am using with the following commands: 

```
git clone https://github.com/aws/aws-codebuild-docker-images.git
cd aws-codebuild-docker-images
cd al2/x86_64/standard/2.0
docker build -t aws/codebuild/amazonlinux2-x86_64-standard:2.0 .
docker run -it --entrypoint sh aws/codebuild/amazonlinux2-x86_64-standard:2.0 -c bash
```
then in that shell:

git clone https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg.git
cd vcpkg
./bootstrap-vcpkg.sh
./vcpkg integrate install
./vcpkg install boost
See error

Although the sed solution allowed me to continue I'm now hitting an error on any package with a patch:
```
Starting package 1/23: liblzma:x64-linux
Building package liblzma[core]:x64-linux...
-- Downloading https://github.com/xz-mirror/xz/archive/v5.2.4.tar.gz...
-- Extracting source /vcpkg/downloads/xz-mirror-xz-v5.2.4.tar.gz
-- Applying patch enable-uwp-builds.patch
CMake Error at scripts/cmake/vcpkg_apply_patches.cmake:52 (message):
  Applying patch failed.  Patch needs to be updated to work with source being
  used by vcpkg!
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  scripts/cmake/vcpkg_extract_source_archive_ex.cmake:134 (vcpkg_apply_patches)
  scripts/cmake/vcpkg_from_github.cmake:139 (vcpkg_extract_source_archive_ex)
  ports/liblzma/portfile.cmake:3 (vcpkg_from_github)
  scripts/ports.cmake:90 (include)


Error: Building package liblzma:x64-linux failed with: BUILD_FAILED
Please ensure you're using the latest portfiles with `.\vcpkg update`, then
submit an issue at https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg/issues including:
  Package: liblzma:x64-linux
  Vcpkg version: 2020.02.04-unknownhash

Additionally, attach any relevant sections from the log files above.
```

 so I assume git is still not being found correctly when this runs also. 

I've since added cmake and ninja to the server manually and symlinked these to `/usr/bin` and although cmake, ninja and git can now be found in the path, when I pass `-useSystemBinaries` during bootstrap and try and run `./vcpkg install liblzma` for example it, still downloads cmake, ninja and reports the git error  again as if the `VCPKG_FORCE_SYSTEM_BINARIES` environment variable is not there. 

Any ideas?

rename.from: vcpkg install returns "A suitable version of git was not found (required v2.7.4)"
rename.to: [docker]vcpkg install returns "A suitable version of git was not found (required v2.7.4)"

body:
use param for installing
`export VCPKG_FORCE_SYSTEM_BINARIES=ON`
and then error with git disappear

I solved this by adding the following to my Dockerfile:
```
ENV VCPKG_FORCE_SYSTEM_BINARIES="1"
```

@armitagemderivitec Please keep this issue open before we resolve it.

Thanks.
